chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Safwan, from Khuzaymah ibn Yaqtin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

«The son of the son (grandson) stands in the place of the son if there is no one from the man's loins [i.e., no direct son].» He said, «And the daughter of the daughter (granddaughter) stands in the place of the daughter if there is no one from the man's loins.»

key_terms.صُلْبُ الرَّجُلِ: Loins of the man (direct male lineage)
key_terms.قَامَ مَقَامَ: Stands in the place of / replaces

ai.seo_question: How does Shia inheritance law treat grandchildren when the deceased has no direct sons or daughters?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *qadam al-maqam* (standing in place), where a grandson or granddaughter inherits as if they were a direct son or daughter, but only in the absence of any direct male or female descendants. This principle ensures that the estate remains within the direct line of descent, distinguishing Shia jurisprudence from other schools where grandsons might share with brothers. It highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the integrity of the primary lineage in inheritance distribution.
